text:
Maya (support): FYI customer reporting intermittent 504s + major latency. They say requests are being served from us-east-1 even though their clients are EU (eu-central-1). Raising for triage.

Priya (prodeng): do we have their sample request id and timestamps?

Maya (support): Yes, req_id=7a9c1f, first_seen=2026-07-03T14:12:02Z. Customer included a curl dump showing header x-served-region: us-east-1 while their geo is eu-central-1.

Jon (eng-sre): paste the raw headers and the routing decision log if you have it.

Maya (support): headers snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
x-served-region: us-east-1
x-routing-reason: capacity_fallback
x-request-id: 7a9c1f
```

routing debug from our tracing (excerpt):

```
route_eval: client_geo=eu-central-1
pool_lookup: prod-eu -> healthy=false
fallback_choice: us-east-1 (latency_budget)
```

Priya (prodeng): We didn't have any regional incident alerts. Jon, can you check the probe health across eu cluster?

Jon (eng-sre): looking now. I see short, frequent probe failures starting ~14:10 UTC. Also noticed the health-probe deployment in eu namespace has HEALTH_PROBE_TTL set to 3 (seconds). Controller expects 90s.

Jon (eng-sre): quick repro/debug I ran:
1) kubectl -n infra get deploy health-probe-eu -o yaml | yq '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[] | select(.name=="HEALTH_PROBE_TTL")'
2) curl -sI -H "Host: api.customer.example" https://api.redwood.example.com/health

Output showed probe env: HEALTH_PROBE_TTL: "3" and probe logs were interpreting transient 2-4s network jitter as hard failures.

Ava (ops): how did TTL become 3? That value is templated in helm/values-prod-eu.yaml

Jon (eng-sre): found a legacy override in infra/helm/values-overrides/eu-experiments.yaml with HEALTH_PROBE_TTL: 3. It was accidentally merged in a maintenance change without follow-up.

Maya (support): customer saw latency jump from ~50ms -> ~260ms and flagged for enterprise support. They asked for repro steps and timeline.

Jon (eng-sre): remediation steps we executed:
- remove stale override and set HEALTH_PROBE_TTL to "90" in values-prod-eu.yaml
- update cluster env quickly: kubectl -n infra set env deployment/health-probe-eu HEALTH_PROBE_TTL=90
- rollout restart the probe deployment in eu with 2-pod canary
- monitor metric probe_success_rate and routing decisions for 20 minutes

Commands used:

```
# fix values and push
git checkout prod
git apply <<'PATCH'
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: infra/helm/values-prod-eu.yaml
@@
-  HEALTH_PROBE_TTL: 3
+  HEALTH_PROBE_TTL: 90
*** End Patch
PATCH
git commit -am "Fix: restore HEALTH_PROBE_TTL to 90s for eu probes"
git push origin prod

# on-cluster quick patch
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/health-probe-eu HEALTH_PROBE_TTL=90
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/health-probe-eu --selector=app=health-probe
```

Priya (prodeng): opened a CI check to assert helm chart TTL matches controller constant. Ticket: https://redwood.example.com/ops/ISSUE-2044

Ava (ops): Finance reported a billing delta coincident with the outage window 2026-07-03T14:10:00Z -> 2026-07-03T14:35:00Z due to cross-region egress. We'll backfill in billing ops.

Jon (eng-sre): after the set-env + canary restart, probe_success_rate recovered from ~78% -> 99.6% within ~7 minutes. Routing returned to eu (x-served-region: eu-central-1) and 504s/latency normalized.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-341 opened for probe TTL override caused multi-region fallback. Linked MR: https://git.redwood.example.com/infra/helm/merge_requests/459

Priya (prodeng): follow-ups:
- add chart CI assertion and alert for cluster-wide capacity=false spikes
- implement a soft fallback window: try short routing retries (probe quiesce window) before full cross-region failover
- run a scan for other env overrides that conflict with controller defaults

Maya (support): updated customer with timeline, root cause (stale helm override), repro steps, and MR link. Customer acknowledged and is satisfied with RCA. :white_check_mark:

Jon (eng-sre): I'll push the CI patch and alert rule today. Closing support thread once MR is merged.
